_readme: CANONICAL SkillBridge resource catalog — the single source of truth. The website renders it, `npm run resources:check` validates it, and `npm run resources:sync` writes a verified snapshot into the content repo for Creator Flow CTA validation. Never hand-edit the snapshot. Only `status: published` items render in production.

friction.age-16: Some steps need you to be 16+

resources.title: Free Career Tools We Recommend
resources.description: A short list of free websites and tools for getting experience, building skills, finding internships, and fixing your resume — plus the ones that look free and are not.
resources.outcome: You get the shortlist we use, all in one file.

source.note: Verified copy, rendered verbatim. Renamed from "Everything We Use" on 2026-07-28 — that title overclaimed. Do not paraphrase the body: edit toolkit.json, then run npm run pdf.

resources.bestFor: You want one place to start

resources.title: Build a Resume Project Without Job Experience
resources.description: Pick a small project you can finish in two weeks, prove what you did, and turn it into a resume bullet.
resources.outcome: You leave with one small project picked and written down.

resources.title: First Internship Application Checklist
resources.description: Check your application before you submit it, use the follow-up message, and know when to move on.
resources.outcome: You leave with a checked application and one message ready to send.

resources.title: 3 Better Networking Questions
resources.description: Use these after someone replies to your LinkedIn message or agrees to a quick call. Each one gets you an answer you cannot Google.
resources.outcome: You leave with one useful answer, one next move, and a reason to follow up.

resources.title: Paid Summer Internships and Jobs for High Schoolers
resources.description: 28 paid summer 2027 programs with the pay, the deadline, and how hard each one is to get.
resources.outcome: You leave knowing which programs you can apply to and which deadline comes first.

resources.title: How to Find a High School Internship
resources.description: Where high school internships come from, which sites are worth checking, and what to do when nobody replies.
resources.outcome: You leave with people to contact and a short message ready to send.

source.note: Adapted from Skyler's Discord guide. Handshake was cut because no source showed high school access. LinkedIn and Indeed age rules checked on their terms pages 2026-11-04.

resources.bestFor: You don't know where to look

resources.title: How to Prepare for Your First Interview
resources.description: What interviewers listen for, how to answer the questions that keep coming up, and how to practice out loud.
resources.outcome: You leave with your stories picked, your answers planned, and questions to ask them.

source.note: Adapted from Skyler's Discord guide plus format tips from the interviewing slides. Arrival time reconciled to five to ten minutes, because the two sources disagreed.

resources.bestFor: You have an interview coming up

resources.title: How to Do Well at Your First Internship
resources.description: What people judge you on, what to ask in your first two weeks, and how to leave with proof of your work.
resources.outcome: You leave with a plan for your first two weeks and a log that turns into resume bullets.

resources.title: 5 Free Credentials for Your Resume
resources.description: Compare five free courses that award a certificate, badge, or credential. Pick one that backs up a project or skill you can show.
resources.outcome: You leave having picked one credential that matches a project.

source.note: All five provider pages re-opened and confirmed live 2026-07-28. Cisco's skillsforall.com now redirects to netacad.com — the catalog and PDF use the current URL.

resources.bestFor: Your resume needs proof of a skill

resources.title: High School Resume Template (No Experience Needed)
resources.description: Edit this one-page Word template, replace the prompts with your own information, and export it as a PDF.
resources.outcome: You leave with a resume you can fill in and export today.

source.note: Opens in Word, Google Docs, or Pages. Written to the corrected editorial rules: city/state only, no street address, ZIP, age, photo, or generic objective.

resources.bestFor: You are writing your first resume

resources.title: AI Tools for School and Job Search
resources.description: See which AI tool to use for studying, resumes, interview practice, outreach, and other common student tasks.
resources.outcome: You stop guessing which tool to open.

source.note: Skyler's AI Tools Guide, updated June 2026. Read-only /preview link — the owner ouid parameter from the original share URL is stripped. Anonymous access confirmed 2026-07-28. Contains its own privacy rule: never paste your full name plus address, passwords, school logins, or family financial info into an AI tool.

resources.bestFor: You need AI for a specific task

resources.title: Build Your First LinkedIn Profile
resources.description: Set up your photo, headline, About section, and experience so your profile does not look empty.
resources.outcome: You leave with a profile someone would want to reply to.

source.note: SkillBridge's own LinkedIn deck. Read-only /preview link. Anonymous access confirmed 2026-07-28. NOTE FOR SKYLER: one headline example on the deck names your club and school. Fine if intentional — say the word and it can be swapped for a neutral example.

resources.title: Blank resume template (Google Doc)
resources.description: The editable Google Doc version of the resume template from the Discord resume drop.
resources.outcome: An editable copy students can make in one click.

source.note: Anonymous access confirmed 2026-07-28 and the OBJECTIVE section has already been removed from the live doc.

resources.blockedReason: The contact line still reads 'City, State Zipcode', which prompts students to publish a ZIP code. The approved editorial rule is city and state only. One edit to that line in the Doc clears this and the item can flip to published — no code change needed.

resources.title: Filled-in example resume (Google Doc)
resources.description: A completed sample resume showing what each section looks like when it is filled in.
resources.outcome: A worked example to compare your own draft against.

source.note: Anonymous access confirmed 2026-07-28. The person in it is fictional, so there is no real-privacy problem.

resources.blockedReason: The example prints a ZIP code ('Los Angeles, California 90024') and leads with a generic objective — the two things the approved editorial rule tells students not to do. Publishing it would teach the opposite of the template. Two edits to the Doc clear it.

resources.title: The Interviewing Pack
resources.description: The interviewing slides, the quick-reference sheet, and the mock-interview prep and scenario from the Discord interviewing drop.
resources.outcome: A full interview-prep set students can work through alone.

source.note: Downloaded from Discord #resource-drops and read 2026-11-04. Fresh copies are in C:/Users/bnark/Downloads.

resources.blockedReason: Read in full on 2026-11-04. Do not re-host as is. The file metadata names a person and our school, the mock scenario looks like a guest speaker's material, and the slides say to arrive 10 minutes early where the Discord guide says 5. The useful parts now live in first-interview-guide. Publish only if Skyler confirms the author is fine with it and the metadata is stripped.

resources.description: The walkthrough deck explaining how each resume section gets reviewed.
resources.outcome: Context for why the template is shaped the way it is.
